overview: LiquidSense's Scaffold is a block-placement module driven by the client event bus. onUpdate handles eagle sneaking, zitter strafing, down-mode sneak suppression and the Tower handoff each tick; onMotion PRE runs update() and findBlock() to select the next target block and rotation, and the place phase (Pre or Post per the PlaceTiming setting) calls place(), which routes the placement through the vanilla player controller so the block leaves as C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement behind a randomized delay. Target selection walks the six faces of the block below the feet over a sampled hit-point grid, ray-traces each candidate twice (occlusion from the eyes and verification that the computed rotation actually faces the neighbor block), and commits the rotation with the smallest difference to the server rotation, applied silently through RotationUtils so the camera never moves while the aimed angles ride the vanilla C03 movement stream. Auto-block modes spoof or switch the held slot with C09PacketHeldItemChange, the swing toggle emits the arm animation as a vanilla swing or an explicit C0APacketAnimation, and the tower modes either hand vertical motion to the Tower companion module or drive a timer-boosted jump from onMotion.

sections.p: Every handler is a separate @EventTarget method. onUpdate runs once per tick: getBestBlocks() refills the hotbar by window-click swapping when Picker is on, the timer speed is applied from the Timer value, the Tower module is toggled on when Tower mode is set and space is held with Speed off, down mode releases the sneak keybind when the sneak bind is held and blocks are available, Slow damps motionX and motionZ, and on the ground the Rewinside mode strafes at 0.2 and zeroes motionY, the smooth zitter alternates the strafe keys every 100ms, the teleport zitter strafes and shifts motion sideways, and eagle runs its BlocksToEagle counter. Eagle in Silent mode emits C0BPacketEntityAction START_SNEAKING or STOP_SNEAKING directly when the sneaking state flips (driven by the air check at feet minus one, or the EdgeDistance per-side gap scan), while Normal mode presses the keybind. onPacket tracks only C09PacketHeldItemChange and stores the last slot id so the Spoof autoblock can skip redundant slot packets. onMotion PRE calls update(), which refuses to run without a block item and calls findBlock(expand), the place phase calls place() when facesBlock is true or RotationMode is Off, and place() resets the delay timer with a fresh randomDelay(MinDelay, MaxDelay) after a successful onPlayerRightClick. onMove requests safe walk when SafeWalk is on, onRender2D draws the block counter, and onDisable restores the sneak state, keys, timer speed and the original hotbar slot via C09.

findBlock anchors on the block under the feet (with a half-block posY correction and a down-mode variant), Expand mode walks candidates up to ExpandLength blocks along the movement input or the horizontal facing, and search() does the real work. For each of the six EnumFacing sides of a replaceable target block it samples the neighbor's clickable surface on a grid stepped by xzRange and yRange divided by the even-rounded SearchAccuracy (calcStepSize floors the step at 0.01), skips samples whose eyes-to-hitVec ray exceeds 18 squared distance, is farther than the far edge of the block, or is occluded by rayTraceBlocks, and derives yaw and pitch from atan2 of the hit vector, with the Static, StaticPitch and StaticYaw modes substituting fixed pitch and yaw offsets. The resulting rotation is validated by ray tracing four blocks along its vector and requiring a block hit on the neighbor; the candidate with the smallest getRotationDifference against serverRotation wins. When MinTurnSpeed is below 180 the chosen rotation goes through RotationUtils.limitAngleChange with a random per-tick cap drawn from [MinTurnSpeed, MaxTurnSpeed], is stored as limitedRotation and lockRotation, and facesBlock is set only if the limited rotation still ray-hits a neighbor; otherwise the raw rotation is applied and facesBlock is set directly. setRotation applies the result through RotationUtils.setTargetRotation when SilentRotation is on, which rewrites the angles that leave in the vanilla C03 packets without moving the camera, or writes rotationYaw and rotationPitch directly; KeepRotation re-applies lockRotation for keepLength ticks.

sections.h: Swing, silent slot switching, tower modes
sections.p: Placement itself is vanilla: place() calls playerController.onPlayerRightClick, which performs the server-bound ray trace and emits C08 through the normal right-click path, and only then resets the delay and dampens motion by SpeedModifier when on the ground. The swing toggle decides the animation: swingValue on calls mc.thePlayer.swingItem() so the vanilla animation logic runs, while swingValue off sends an explicit C0APacketAnimation, which still resets the swing cooldown and keeps the server-side animation stream consistent. AutoBlock Off refuses placement when no block item is held; Spoof sends C09PacketHeldItemChange(blockSlot - 36) only when the tracked slot (updated in onPacket) differs, so the server-held slot stays whatever it was while the client actually places with the inventory slot; Switch sends the C09 on every placement; the third branch additionally calls playerController.updateController(). onDisable always restores the original slot with a final C09. The tower modes produce the vertical motion: Tower mode fakes mc.thePlayer.onGround = false and toggles the Tower companion module, which climbs with its own jump, motion, packet or teleport modes; TowerMove runs in onMotion, zeroing motionX, motionZ and jumpMovementFactor, and when the block below is air with a targetPlace set it applies motionY = 0.4196 (the vanilla jump impulse), multiplies horizontal motion by 0.75, and with TowerBoost sets mc.timer.timerSpeed to 5F, so each game tick advances the column five times faster than normal while the placement pipeline keeps up.

files.label: Scaffold.java (module logic)
files.explanation: The entire module lives in this one file. The value block at the top defines the full configurable surface: Mode, MinDelay and MaxDelay plus the PlaceableDelay re-arm toggle, AutoBlock, Sprint, Swing, Search, Down, Picker, PlaceTiming, the three eagle modes with BlocksToEagle and EdgeDistance, the Expand sub-modes, RotationStrafe, the four rotation modes with SilentRotation and KeepRotation, static pitch and yaw offsets, the xz and y search ranges, SearchAccuracy, the Min and MaxTurnSpeed window, zitter, timer, SpeedModifier, sameY, safe walk, air safe, and the tower switches. The six event handlers that follow are the pipeline: onUpdate runs the per-tick behavior (eagle, zitter, down, slow, Rewinside, tower handoff), onMotion PRE runs update() and the place phase runs place(), onPacket tracks the held slot from C09, onMove requests safe walk, and the two render handlers draw the overlay. findBlock, search and place are the core: findBlock picks the anchor position and expand candidates, search samples hit points, verifies occlusion and rotation rays and commits the least-turning rotation, and place drives onPlayerRightClick and the delay, swing, autoblock and motion-damp side effects. Reading the file top to bottom therefore gives the config surface, the timing logic, and the packet-emitting core in that order.

files.label: RotationUtils.java (silent rotation and aim math)
files.explanation: RotationUtils is the shared math layer every rotation-consuming module in the client funnels through. serverRotation holds the last server-confirmed rotation and targetRotation the pending silent one; setTargetRotation feeds the silent-rotation pipeline that rewrites the yaw and pitch leaving in the movement packets without moving the camera, which is how the scaffold aims at the block below while the player looks straight ahead. limitAngleChange clamps a rotation to a maximum per-tick delta against the current rotation, which the scaffold invokes with a random cap between Min and MaxTurnSpeed so the server-observed rotation turns at a randomized, bounded rate. getRotationDifference scores a candidate rotation against serverRotation and drives the scaffold's choice of the least-turning face, while getVectorForRotation converts the committed rotation into a direction vector for the four-block verification ray in search(). applyStrafeToPlayer rewrites the strafe and forward input in the StrafeEvent and powers the RotationStrafe mode. The class is shared with the Aura and Tower modules, so a rotation-pattern analysis of this client reads the same angle stream the scaffold writes.

countering.label: FastPlace (placement rate window)
countering.explanation: NCP runs its blockplace checks from BlockPlaceListener.onBlockPlace. FastPlace scores every placement into data.fastPlaceBuckets, an ActionFrequency with two 1000ms buckets (BlockPlaceData line 53), and takes the fullScore of the window; a violation fires when fullScore exceeds cc.fastPlaceLimit (default 15, DefaultConfig line 183). A parallel short-term counter counts placements within cc.fastPlaceShortTermTicks (default 10 ticks) against cc.fastPlaceShortTermLimit (default 6), with the count lag-adjusted through TickTask.getLag. The accumulated fastPlaceVL feeds the action list, which cancels from vl>5 and escalates through vl>20 and vl>80 to a kick at the top tier, and once fastPlaceVL passes 25 the Improbable feed (weight 0.3 by default) layers a statistical check on top. The module's exposure is direct: with MinDelay 0 and MaxDelay 0 every motion tick places one block, about 20 per second, so each one-second bucket scores around 20 against a limit of 15 and the 10-tick short-term window sees around 10 placements against a limit of 6, flagging both paths. The MinDelay and MaxDelay randomization is the module's own mitigation: a delay of 100ms halves the rate to about 10 per second, which sits under the 15 bucket limit and at the 6-per-10-tick short-term edge, so the Improbable feed becomes the deciding layer because a regular cadence still scores as improbable. Note that NCP skips the Against check for scaffolding material, but FastPlace runs for every placement regardless of material.

countering.label: Direction (look ray vs clicked block)
countering.explanation: The blockplace Direction check extends AbstractBlockDirectionCheck and runs from BlockPlaceListener.onBlockPlace (lines 322-332) against the server-tracked look. It casts a ray from the player's eye (foot location plus eye height) along the direction stored in the flying queue: BoulderChecker.checkFlyingQueue replays the look across the recent C03 and C06 packets and intersects the ray with the clicked block's AABB expanded by 0.1 via CollideRayVsAABB; a miss yields the closest squared distance as the violation measure and addVL accumulates it into the blockplace VL with the configured actions (default cancel). A second gate, isInteractable, rejects the placement when the clicked face is not reachable from the player's position relative to the block, for example clicking the far side of a full block. The scaffold is built to satisfy this check: search() only commits a rotation after ray tracing four blocks along it and confirming the hit lands on the neighbor, and silent rotation writes those exact angles into the C03 stream the flying queue replays, so a correctly aimed placement passes. The failure modes are the static modes and the turn-speed limiter: StaticPitch and StaticYaw substitutes only commit when their fixed angles still ray-hit the block, and when MinTurnSpeed is below 180 the limited rotation is accepted only if it still faces a neighbor, so an overly slow turn cap simply prevents placement (facesBlock stays false) instead of producing an off-block placement Direction would flag. With RotationMode Off the module places with the player's own look, which only survives while the player keeps the block under the crosshair, and the visible snap of non-silent rotation still carries the same aim, so Direction passes but the snap itself is exposed to aim-pattern checks.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (vertical envelope vs tower modes)
countering.explanation: The tower modes assert vertical motion, and NCP's SurvivalFly bounds it from the world rather than the packet. check() (line 114) derives the vertical allowance from vDistRel (line 1839), which seeds the allowed y distance from the previous move's momentum (lastMove.yDistance) and accepts a jump only when the player was actually grounded: fromOnGround and toOnGround come from RichBoundsLocation.isOnGround(), a block scan at minY minus yOnGround, never from the packet's onGround flag. The violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 with a set-back to the stored location. The scaffold's Tower mode hands off to the Tower companion, whose Jump mode re-applies the 0.42 impulse every tick when JumpDelay is 0: after the first jump the player is in air, so each re-impulse presents a positive yDistance with no grounded origin, vDistRel has no momentum to credit, and the first in-air re-jump accumulates yDistanceAboveLimit and violates. TowerMove's motionY = 0.4196 is a single vanilla jump, which the envelope accepts once, but TowerBoost's mc.timer.timerSpeed = 5F compresses five ticks of movement into one real second of packets: the client sends roughly five times the normal C03 rate and the server-side position advances a full tick per processed move, so the per-move envelope and the separate MorePackets rate check both engage. NCP does contain an explicit accommodation for scaffold play: the ground-appeared branch (lines 159-166) adjusts the set-back location when a block placement creates the ground the player lands on, so legitimately placed columns do not cascade set-backs, but the vertical envelope itself is unchanged.

countering.label: Arc v2 BLOCK_PLACE handling (soup AutoHeal only; no placement validation)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's only C08 consumption is in PacketListener.onPacketReceiving (lines 134-146): every BLOCK_PLACE packet is wrapped as WrapperPlayClientBlockPlace, the held item is read, and only a mushroom-soup item feeds the AutoHeal check. There is no placement-rate, direction, reach or no-swing check anywhere in the Arc v2 check tree (only the combat, inventory, management and moving categories exist), so the scaffold's placement stream is entirely unvalidated: the C08 cadence, the clicked face and the silent-rotation aim are never inspected. The pressure on this module from Arc v2 comes from the movement layer instead. The tower's Timer 5F raises the vanilla C03 flow to roughly 100 move packets per second, and MorePackets (config.yml max-packets 30, max-packets-kick 70) counts flying and position packets per second, cancelling all movement packets above 30 and kicking above 70, so a boosted tower trip is caught by the rate counter even though the placement itself is ignored. The Tower companion's packet and teleport modes add explicit C04 position packets that inflate the same counters, and Flight rejects vertical motion beyond the jump envelope when those modes climb too fast.
